neutral_facts.value: The accused, who was married to the victim, was involved in a marital dispute with the victim. The victim was subjected to mental and physical cruelty by the accused, including harassment over the demand for dowry. The victim committed suicide by setting herself on fire in their home within a year of marriage. The accused reported the incident to the police, and an FIR was registered. The victim's body showed signs of burns and injuries consistent with the act of self-immolation. The prosecution alleged that the accused had demanded dowry and subjected the victim to harassment, leading to her suicide. The trial court acquitted the accused, but the High Court overturned this decision, finding that the evidence supported the prosecution's case.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the deceased was subjected to mental and physical cruelty by the appellant due to dowry demands, leading to her suicide by setting herself on fire. The appellant had demanded dowry in the form of cash and ornaments, and the deceased was subjected to harassment over the balance of dowry. The deceased's suicide was within one year of marriage, and the death was caused by burns and bodily injury, which falls under the definition of dowry death.

quotes.text: The prosecution case in a nutshell is that one Smt. Leelavati was married to the appellant on 16.4.1989 and was living in the house of the appellant at Konanakunte in Bangalore. Besides attending the household chores, she was gainfully employed in a private company.
The deceased had been subjected to mental and physical torture over certain issues including the one for demand of balance of dowry.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the deceased's suicide was not due to dowry harassment but rather due to personal reasons, such as not conceiving after marriage. They contended that the witnesses were biased and that the evidence did not establish harassment or cruelty by the appellant. The accused also claimed that the dowry was given as a gift and not as dowry, and that the recovery of ornaments was not properly established.

quotes.text: The accused-appellant has stated as under:- 'We belong to kodava community. In our community there is no custom of giving and taking dowry. In our community half the expenses is borne by the bridegroom and half is borne by the bride's side. I have never demanded dowry, I have not harassed my wife for bringing dowry. The witnesses are giving false deposition.'

It is further contended that the High Court has drawn the presumption under Section 113-B of the Indian Evidence Act though the ingredients of the offences were not proved and it was not shown by the prosecution that the appellant treated the deceased with such cruelty and subjected her to such harassment to drive her to commit suicide.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that under Section 304-B of the IPC, a dowry death is presumed to have been caused by the husband or his relatives if the death occurs within seven years of marriage and the deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment related to dowry demands. The Court also relied on Sections 113-A and 113-B of the Evidence Act, which provide presumptions regarding abetment of suicide and dowry death.

quotes.text: Section 304-B, IPC applies where the death of a woman is caused by any burns, bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances, within seven years of her marriage and the cause of death is because the women was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or her husband's family or relatives and such harassment should be in relation to a demand of dowry.
The Court may presume, having regard to all the other circumstances of the case, that such suicide had been abetted by her husband or by such relative of her husband.

Bansi Lal vs. State of Haryana, (2011) 11 SCC 359, observed: 'It may be mentioned herein that the legislature in its wisdom has used the word 'shall' thus, making a mandatory application on the part of the court to presume that death had been committed by the person who had subjected her to cruelty or harassment in connection with any demand of dowry.'

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the High Court found the trial court's acquittal to be perverse and based on conjectures. The Court held that the evidence established the deceased's harassment and cruelty by the appellant, leading to her dowry death, and that the presumption under Section 304-B IPC was not rebutted.

The High Court has correctly recorded the finding based on evidence and found the appellant guilty of commission of offence.

other_sentence_order.value: The Court directed the appellant to return the dowry amount of Rs 15,000/- and the gold ornaments, failing which, an amount equal to their value plus Rs 15,000/- may be recovered as fine.
